From **top to bottom,** the $y$-intercepts of the hyperbola $9{y}^{2}-4{x}^{2}=36$ are

$($
{{field-1}}, 
{{field-2}} $)\,$
and
$\,($
{{field-3}}, 
{{field-4}} $).$
feedback.worked_solution:
To find the $y$-intercepts of the hyperbola, we substitute $x=0$ into the equation of the hyperbola and solve for $y,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}9{y}^{2}-4{x}^{2} & =36 \\ 9{y}^{2}-4(0)^{2} & =36 \\ 9{y}^{2} & =36 \\ {y}^{2} & =4 \\ y & =\pm 2\end{aligned}
$$

So, from top to bottom, the $y$-intercepts are $(0,2)$ and $(0,-2).$
